page: Microsoft Azure F64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Faldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The server is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 7559 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the F64alds_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% across multiple categories. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench confirm high processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only small block and large block read/write operations, also rank in the top 10%. The processor's instruction set support, including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI, enables rapid execution of specialized tasks. This is reflected in top-tier scores for software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the F64alds_v7 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per core, which limits its suitability for memory-bound applications. However, this resource allocation provides high compute density and qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-heavy workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. The inclusion of 7559 GB of local storage offsets external storage dependency for data-intensive operations. This server is configured for workloads such as high-throughput web serving, software compilation, text and image processing, and medium-scale LLM inference.
